tagline.text: A big Quezon City mall sitting on top of the northern end of the MRT line

location.label: Location
location.text: Corner of EDSA and North Avenue, Bagong Pag-asa, Quezon City

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~2,500 (per person for meals, transport and shopping)

children.text: TriNoma is a large Ayala Malls shopping center in Quezon City, linked directly to MRT-3 North Avenue station by a footbridge. It is a good place to shop, eat, watch a movie and stroll a rooftop park in one stop, and a new building, The Exchange at TriNoma, opened in October 2026.

TriNoma is a large shopping mall at the corner of EDSA and North Avenue in Quezon City, Metro Manila. During construction it was known as the North Triangle Commercial Center before being renamed TriNoma, and it is operated by Ayala Malls, part of Ayala Land. According to Wikipedia, it soft-opened in May 2007 and held its grand opening on October 16 of the same year. With about 124,000 visitors a day, it is one of the main shopping hubs of northern Metro Manila.

What makes this mall unusual is that it sits on top of a transit depot. The MRT-3 train depot is beneath the building, and the mall was built above it. That is why the MRT-3 North Avenue station connects to the mall by a link bridge built in 2007, so you can step off the train and walk into the mall without getting rained on. For travelers moving around Quezon City in the rainy season, this is its biggest advantage.

The mall has four main shopping levels and two smaller ones, and its anchor is The Landmark, a combined supermarket and department store. Clothing, accessories and electronics shops, a food court, restaurants, cinemas, bookstores, pharmacies and service shops are all gathered here, which makes it a handy base for a day out. Korean families and students living in Quezon City also often choose it as a meeting spot.

On October 30, 2026, a new building called The Exchange at TriNoma opened on the North Avenue side. It is a mixed shopping and transport complex, with shops, restaurants and service outlets plus a terminal that gathers buses and UV Express vans. It is expected to connect later to a unified central station linking MRT-3, MRT-7 and LRT-1, so the area will keep changing over the next few years. There are also places of worship such as the St. Michael the Archangel Chapel on the second floor, which gives you a feel for a typical Philippine mall. The reason to feature this mall as a destination is that it is the easiest way to experience everyday Philippine mall culture. Filipinos eat, watch movies, attend Mass and hold family gatherings in malls to escape the heat and rain. At TriNoma you can watch this for free, and if you come and go by MRT you will also see local commuter life. It is not a sightseeing spot with one big attraction, though, so it works best as a relaxed stop between other plans.

From MRT-3 North Avenue station, you walk along the link bridge straight into the mall. Because it is the end of the line, getting here from Makati and Ayala is simple, and you can move around without getting wet even in the rainy season.

Above the mall is a two-level park of about one hectare. With open-air restaurants, a performance stage and water gardens, it is a pleasant place to rest between shopping stops. It is especially busy on cooler evenings.

blocks.title: The Landmark department store and supermarket

children.text: This is the mall's anchor store, where you can buy household goods, clothing and groceries all at once. It is convenient for stocking up on water, snacks and daily items for your accommodation. Stock and the range of goods change from time to time, so check on site.
The mall has several cinemas, and after renovations in 2024-2025 new screens such as A-Luxe and A-Giant cinemas have opened. For showtimes and prices, a booking app is the most accurate source.

blocks.title: Many restaurants and a food court

children.text: From fast food to Japanese, Korean and cafes, the choice is wide. Lines can be long at mealtimes, so going around two in the afternoon or early in the evening is much calmer.

This new building opened on October 30, 2026, with shoe, bookstore, electronics, cafe and beauty shops arriving first. Some stores are still preparing to open, so check the official announcements before you visit.

blocks.title: The MRT-3 terminus and commuter culture

children.text: North Avenue is the northern end station of MRT-3 and was part of the first section that opened on December 15, 1999. On the platform and on the footbridge you can watch Manila commuters at close range during their daily trips.
Two parking buildings and open-air lots together are reported to hold about 8,000 cars. It is convenient for drivers, but cars back up at the entrances on weekends and at year-end.

items.subtitle: Arrive by MRT, then shop, eat and stroll the park

children.text: Get off at MRT-3 North Avenue station and walk along the link bridge into the mall. The mall usually opens between

Look around The Landmark and the first and second floor shops, and buy what you need first. It is better to finish shopping before you are carrying too many bags.
Have lunch at the food court or a restaurant. Half past twelve is the busiest time, so if you can, eat an hour earlier.
Head to The Exchange, the newly opened building, to browse the new stores and cafes.
Go up to the rooftop TriNoma Park to stroll and rest.
Take MRT-3 back before the rush hour. On weekday evenings, from

The timetable is only an example. If you have a movie planned, shift things around it, and check the mall's opening hours in the official announcements before you go.

items.title: Full-day course
items.subtitle: A loop around northern Quezon City

children.text: Take a morning walk at Quezon Memorial Circle. It is a short drive from TriNoma.
Move to TriNoma and have lunch.
Spend time shopping and resting at a cafe.
Have dinner at the rooftop park or a restaurant in the mall, then watch a movie.
If the movie ends late, check the last MRT train. Late at night, Grab is more convenient.

items.title: From the airport and from Manila by air

children.text: From Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL) to Quezon City takes about
40 minutes to 1 hour 30 minutes
by car. It depends heavily on traffic.
Take Grab or a taxi and enter "TriNoma" or "North Avenue EDSA" as the destination. At the airport, use only the official taxi stands.
Taking the MRT from the airport involves many transfers across the city, so it is not recommended if you have luggage.

MRT-3 runs along EDSA, and its northern terminus is North Avenue station, which connects to TriNoma by a footbridge. Because it is the end of the line, you can come in one ride from Ayala and Buendia stations in Makati.
The schedule is listed as roughly
for the first train and

for the last weekday train, but it can change, so check the latest DOTr announcements. The regular fare from North Avenue to Taft Avenue is about ₱28, and there are reports that a half-price discount has applied since March 2026, so check the station notices.
EDSA bus stops and Quezon City Bus Service routes reach TriNoma. There is a bus transfer area inside the mall that connects to suburban routes.
The commuter terminal at The Exchange is due to start operating at the end of 2026, with 13 routes.

Around the mall, use Grab, taxis or tricycles. The footbridge that used to lead to the nearby SM City North EDSA has been closed to make way for the MRT-7 station, so assume it no longer connects on foot and check how to get there separately.
Because it is an indoor mall, weather rarely forces you to change plans. The MRT platform and footbridge are outdoors, though, so you will be exposed to some heat and rain.

At the end of the year the mall is busy with Christmas decorations, and weekday evenings and weekend afternoons are the most crowded. For a quiet visit, we recommend weekday mornings or early afternoons.

At year-end the mall is decorated for Christmas and packed with people buying gifts. As of November 2026 Ayala Malls has started Christmas events at malls nationwide, but we could not confirm a separate TriNoma event schedule, so check the official social media pages before you go.

You can have both lunch and dinner inside the mall. At The Exchange, ramen, malatang, bubble tea, bakery and coffee shops opened first, while some fast food chains and Starbucks were reported as preparing to open. Which stores are open changes from time to time.

There is no hotel inside the mall, so you stay at hotels around Quezon City and along EDSA. You can also stay in Makati or Ortigas along the MRT line and come for a day trip. Check recent reviews of your lodging before you leave.

A few more dining tips. At lunch the food court is easy on the budget and offers lots of choices, so even a group can find something for everyone. In the evening the open-air restaurants near the rooftop park have a nice atmosphere, but on rainy days the indoor shops are better. If you have children, the food court is handy, with seating and restrooms close by. Korean restaurants are more common outside the mall in Quezon City or Makati, so if you need Korean food, check the tenant list in the official announcements first.
When you come by MRT, follow the footbridge from North Avenue station straight into the mall. Follow the station signs so you do not get confused about which exit to take.
Avoid the MRT at weekday rush hour (17:00-19:00), when it is extremely crowded.
The mall's hours are often listed as 10:00-21:00 on weekdays and 10:00-22:00 from Friday to Sunday, but they differ by source, so check the official announcements.
The Landmark supermarket is handy for daily supplies and snacks for your accommodation, but its range of goods changes often.
Book movie seats in advance on an app and check the cinema type.
The new Exchange building is still filling with tenants, so there are more places to see all the time.
At year-end, arrive early because gift shopping and events bring big crowds.
On hot days it is cool inside the mall, so a light jacket is handy.
The mall is big with many floors, so if you get lost, check the floor map on the directory first and agree on a meeting place.
Crowds at the MRT platform and mall entrances raise the risk of pickpockets, so carry your bag in front.
Watch your phone and wallet in crowded MRT cars and at mall entrances.
At the airport, use only official taxis or Grab and avoid touts.
In the rainy season, roads can flood and slow your trip.
Some areas are under construction and routes change, so follow the signs.
Opening hours, fares and last-train times change often, so check the latest announcements before you go.
Money changers or ATMs inside the mall may have long lines at some times, so prepare cash in advance.
A large park near TriNoma, about
10-30 minutes
away by car depending on traffic. It is good for a morning walk and outdoor activities.
A mixed-use district in eastern Quezon City with restaurants and a nightlife street. If you combine it with TriNoma, taking Grab is recommended.
A well-known spot for a different style of shopping; it is far enough that it works better as a separate outing.
A large mall south along EDSA, reachable via the MRT and EDSA, so it is a good way to continue shopping.
